_comment: Ships WITH the plugin. An adopter installs Project-OS and the protocol injects itself — nobody edits their own settings.json, which is the per-repo wiring step that silently never happened. Every command is fully guarded and ends in `|| true`: a broken or absent Project-OS state must never break someone's session.

hooks.command: [ -f .project-os/meta.json ] && [ "$(node -p "JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('.project-os/meta.json','utf8')).docsVerifiedAtCommit" 2>/dev/null)" != "$(git rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null)" ] && echo "[Project-OS] The documentation was last verified against a different commit than HEAD, so it is behind the code. Run the freshness check (see .project-os/config.json 'verify') and write whatever it reports as owed, before adding new work on top." || true
